title: Cone of vision setback from a bedroom or study major opening: 3 m
text: For development adjoining an existing dwelling. C3.9.1 All sources of overlooking are oriented, offset or setback in accordance with Table 3.9a so that the cone of vision (refer Figure 3.9a) does not capture major openings and/or active habitable spaces on an adjoining property (refer Figure 3.9b). Table 3.9a Cone of vision radius (type of habitable room/active habitable space with a floor level of more than 0.5m above natural ground level): Major opening from bedroom and study: 3m.

exceptions.label: cone of vision does not capture a major opening or active habitable space of the adjoining existing dwelling

replaces.note: R50 and lower 4.5 / 6 / 7.5 m -> 3 / 4.5 / 6 m; R60 unchanged

notes: from: ch3 C3.10.1-r1 (renumbered C3.9.1; Table 3.9a 3.0 m, literal in the evaluator). Where the cone does not capture an adjoining opening or active habitable space the clause is satisfied (exception). Applies to sources with a floor level more than 0.5 m above NGL; the cone radius includes the width of any adjoining ROW, communal street or battleaxe leg (p45 note). C3.9.4 applies C3.9.1-C3.9.3 between apartments on the same lot. Vacant or unknown adjoining sites are C3.9.5. R10-R50 apartments gain 1.5 m per category.
